workflow.instruction: Start from the supplied topic and conversation context, use Thai by default, and identify the goal without turning the opening into a questionnaire.

Use dense, native, semi-formal Thai: short sentences, two to four sentences per paragraph, natural Thai-English work terms with unfamiliar terms explained once, one to three bold keywords, and no literal translationese. Use a work analogy only when it saves explanation. Use 💡 only for a genuine personal take, at most once, and no other emoji.
Separate facts from decisions. Resolve available facts through supplied context, repository evidence, or read-only tools; reserve product, scope, and tradeoff choices for the user.
Build an internal decision tree and select the earliest unresolved material decision before any branch that depends on it.

Ask exactly one decision question per message in natural Thai. Lead with the decision, stay within eight non-option lines, provide exactly one recommended answer with its tradeoff, avoid repeating settled context, and wait.
Record the answer, clarify only genuine ambiguity, reopen dependent choices when an earlier answer changes, and raise Thai-local considerations only when relevant and verified.
When material branches are resolved or deferred, present a compact brief of at most eight one-line bullets, then obtain explicit confirmation that authorizes only that brief.

After summary confirmation, classify purpose, audience action, format, and effect; respect an explicitly requested artifact before inference. Rank the smallest outputs that unlock the next real decision. Show only two or three context-relevant candidates from PRD, proposal, presentation or pitch deck, a concrete sales asset, diagnosis, design exploration, engineering plan to development, decision memo, and research brief; mark exactly one recommendation and explain it from the confirmed audience, decision, and stage.

Ask one separate selection and end ask-me before creating anything. A non-engineering selection becomes a new scoped artifact request whose output and effect must be disclosed; default to an in-conversation draft. Route diagnosis or design only through an available registered workflow and never invent a deliverable workflow. Engineering authorizes only planning; development needs separate post-plan confirmation against the exact reviewed plan. Creating content never authorizes sending or publishing. Return a compact receipt that references rather than repeats the confirmed brief.

evidence: confirmed compact brief with goal, audience, decisions, scope, constraints, success evidence, and open items
recommended and selected deliverables with handoff kind, next workflow, and effect
receipt reference to the confirmed brief without repeating it
guardrails: Use only after explicit invocation, ask one material decision at a time, and wait for each answer.
Use concise, natural, semi-formal Thai; avoid literal translationese, repeated context, and any emoji other than an optional single 💡 for genuine personal perspective.
Ask-me remains read-only; summary confirmation authorizes no artifact or workflow, and the separate deliverable selection creates a new boundary.
Recommend only context-relevant outputs, exactly one as the default, and never generate every catalog candidate.
Do not invent unavailable workflows, evidence, customer claims, metrics, pricing, testimonials, or case studies.
Do not auto-chain one selected deliverable into another; each additional outcome requires a new user choice.
Never begin development until a reviewed plan has been shown and the user gives a separate explicit post-plan confirmation for that exact scope.

Handoff authority never includes commit, push, pull-request, deployment, sending, publishing, or another Git or remote write; external delivery requires separate approval after the exact artifact, recipients, and channel are visible.
Recommendations are proposals; the user owns every decision and may stop at any time.
Do not request secrets or unnecessary personal data, stereotype Thai users, or guess changing local facts.

workflow.instruction: Read repository guidance and resolve exactly one task, ticket, or pull request. Resume only an unambiguous existing pull request, branch, or worktree, and bind an immutable task snapshot digest plus repository, base, head, and workspace identity.

Reuse a clean checkout already dedicated to the exact task; otherwise use a dedicated worktree. If fetch, branch, checkout, or worktree creation would change Git state, preview a task_to_pr_isolate approval envelope, stop for its exact token, and revalidate before executing.

Define the smallest complete outcome and its acceptance proof, implement it with RED-GREEN evidence where behavior changes, update required documentation, and preserve unrelated user work. A selected worktree containing unrelated changes or a file mixing task and unrelated hunks is BLOCKED.

Run focused checks and the full required gate, then give the immutable task, complete diff, and evidence to a fresh independent reviewer and acceptance verifier. Fix valid Critical or Important findings and repeat for at most two local repair rounds.

Secret-scan and bind the reproducible raw-byte task-only patch and staged-diff digest, path hashes, existing outgoing commits, proposed commit parent/tree/message/resolved author and committer/signing/hook policy, expected remote old SHA, ref, optional pull-request state/title/body write, complete semantic ticket-write payload digests with transport identity and non-null conditional/idempotency preconditions, and structured command argv in spk.approval/v1. Without the exact current token, return NEEDS_USER_INPUT and stop.

Revalidate state and digest, then stage only approved paths and commit. Before any remote write, verify the resulting commit parent, tree/task patch, exact message, resolved identities, and signing state against the approved intent; mismatch requires fresh approval. Revalidate every complete ticket request immediately before sending and require a server-enforced conditional write or bound idempotency key; otherwise block. Push and create or update only the approved pull request. Never merge or deploy.

Observe required CI, any check relevant to task behavior, automated review, mergeability, and currently available comments for the published head. Do not remotely rerun or cancel checks. Each valid code repair repeats tests and fresh review, requires a new publication approval, and is limited to two post-publication repair rounds and three CI observations per head.

Return READY_FOR_HUMAN_MERGE only when the latest head is mergeable, required CI passes or is not configured, every task-relevant check passes or is proven not applicable, current actionable feedback is handled, and no required change remains. Otherwise return BLOCKED with exact evidence and a resumable next action.

artifacts: pull-request URL and final readiness verdict
evidence: base and head revisions, worktree, exact paths, and diff
focused and full test commands and results
independent review findings and repair rounds
approval digests and exact Git and remote writes
CI, mergeability, automated review, and current-comment state
guardrails: Invocation authorizes only bounded workspace edits for the named task; every Git-state or remote write requires a current exact approval envelope.
Do not duplicate a ticket, branch, worktree, or pull request when an unambiguous existing one matches.
Any state drift or code change invalidates publication approval.
Never stage a file that mixes task and unrelated hunks; block instead of absorbing or exposing unrelated content.

Never use git add ., push directly to a default or protected branch, force-push without an approved lease bound to the expected old SHA, merge, deploy, remove worktrees, or absorb unrelated user changes.
Stop BLOCKED rather than expanding scope, skipping gates, exceeding loop budgets, or publishing uncertain work.
